newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Novus shares spring back from selloff.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Novus shares spring back from selloff.

text.p: Shares in oil and gas group, Novus Petroleum Ltd, jumped to an intraday high of A$3.30 on Thursday, up over 15 percent in the past two days as the company continues to recover from the selldown from the record highs of a month ago.

The company reported a sharply higher year operating profit of A$44.31 million on Wednesday and brokers said the profit had been the turning point for investor sentiment on the stock rather than the driving force behind the rise.

"It wasn't so much yesterday's result, which was in line with expectations, but their full exploration book and the potential purchase from WMC (of their Australian petroleum assets)," said a Melbourne-based broker, noting that company executives had recently been on a roadshow to investors.

On February 26, 1997, Novus was named as preferred bidder for the Australian petroleum assets of major miner WMC Ltd, a portfolio that includes joint venture interests in a number of exploration and production licences in the Carnarvon Basin offshore Western Australia.

Novus shares listed in May 1995 and reached a record high of A$3.45 on February 9, 1997, although they suffered a selldown from there to a 1997 low of A$2.83 on March 4, from which point the shares commmenced the climb back to today's levels.
"They have been a bit oversold so you have seen a rebound there as well," the broker said.
By 3.30 p.m. (0430 GMT), Novus shares were 31 cents higher at A$3.26 on turnover of 256,684 shares.
